minutes.headline: Select Board issued a suspended cease-and-desist to Conrad's over back taxes and pulled four lots from the lien sale.
minutes.summary: The meeting opened with a member's public comment criticizing the Architectural Preservation District Commission's delays on the 30 School Street demolition. The board then made several appointments, approved pole petitions and a skate park toll booth, and discussed trash service on private roads. It voted a conditional cease-and-desist for Conrad's, removed four properties from the tax lien sale, and reviewed the draft annual town meeting warrant.

what_happened.line: The Select Board voted to send Conrad's a cease-and-desist, effective March 15 unless taxes are paid in full or a payment arrangement is made.
The board voted to remove four properties from the tax lien sale list.
The board reviewed the draft annual town meeting warrant, settling on one combined article for demolition and design plans for 30 School Street, plus a placeholder article on the APDC bylaw.
Trash service on private roads ended with no resolution; the town manager is to forward the contract and seek a timeline from the hauler.
The board approved two pole petitions, a skate park toll booth fundraiser permit, and several appointments, and continued a third pole petition to the next week.

why_it_matters: Unpaid property taxes on a commercial property now carry a dated enforcement step, and the lien sale list that collects overdue bills was shortened by four properties.
The warrant articles drafted here, including the 30 School Street demolition and design article, are what town meeting voters will be asked to take a vote on.
Whether the town provides trash service on private roads is unsettled and tied to the hauler's contract, so residents on those roads have no answer yet.
watch_next: March 15, the date the Conrad's cease-and-desist takes effect unless taxes are paid or an arrangement is made.
The continued Kilburn Street pole petition (plan 971-L), due back at the board the following week.

reconciliation.what: Our minutes against the minutes the town published. caption_error = the same fact the captions rendered badly, resolved by the official reading shown beside the as-heard one; discrepancy = a substantive difference, flagged and not resolved. Neither record is treated as the referee.
reconciliation.summary: The two records agree on all nine non-procedural votes and on most budget figures. Differences are mostly caption misreadings of names and digits. The main exceptions are the Dispatch dollar figure, the APDC bylaw decision, and several items only one record has.
